name: Koshary
description: Egypt's beloved national dish — a hearty mix of rice, lentils, pasta, and chickpeas topped with a spiced tomato sauce and crispy fried onions.
steps: Cook lentils in salted water until tender, then drain.
Cook rice separately and mix with lentils while warm.
Boil macaroni until al dente, drain and set aside.
Fry sliced onions in oil until deeply golden and crispy. Remove and drain.
In the same pan, sauté garlic, add crushed tomatoes, vinegar, cumin, salt, and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes.
To serve: layer rice-lentil mix, then macaroni, then chickpeas.
Top with tomato sauce and crispy onions.

name: Molokhya
description: A rich, velvety green soup made from jute leaves, simmered with chicken broth and finished with a fragrant garlic and coriander ta'leya.
steps: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot.
Add frozen molokhya and stir until fully thawed and simmering.
Season with salt and simmer on low for 5 minutes.
Crush garlic with a pinch of salt until it forms a paste.
Melt butter in a small pan, add garlic paste and ground coriander. Fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour the garlic ta'leya into the soup and stir immediately.
Serve hot over white rice with a side of chicken and bread.

name: Macarona Bashamel
description: Egypt's iconic baked pasta — layers of macaroni and spiced minced meat smothered in a thick, creamy béchamel sauce and baked until golden.
steps: Cook pasta until al dente, drain and set aside.
Sauté diced onion until soft, add minced beef and cook until browned. Stir in tomato paste, salt, and pepper.
Make béchamel: melt butter, whisk in flour for 1 minute, then gradually add milk whisking constantly until thick.
Remove béchamel from heat, season with nutmeg and salt, then beat in eggs quickly.
In a greased baking dish layer: half the pasta, all the meat, remaining pasta.
Pour béchamel over the top, spreading evenly.
Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes until the top is deep golden.

name: Chicken Ranch
description: Tender grilled chicken marinated in ranch spices, served with a tangy homemade ranch dipping sauce and fresh vegetables.
steps: Mix olive oil, garlic powder, onion powder, dill, parsley, paprika, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Score the chicken breasts and coat thoroughly with the marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.
Grill over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through.
Let rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Serve with ranch dipping sauce and a fresh salad.

name: Macarona bil Lahma
description: A comforting Egyptian stovetop pasta — macaroni simmered in a rich, spiced tomato and beef sauce until it soaks up all the flavour.
steps: Sauté diced onion and garlic in oil until golden.
Add minced beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in tomato sauce, 7-spice, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add raw macaroni to the sauce with enough water to cover by 2cm.
Cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until pasta is tender and sauce is absorbed.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot.
